newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan reveals Lasmo gas find in Sindh province.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan reveals Lasmo gas find in Sindh province.

text.p: Pakistan said Monday that British explorer Lasmo had found a gas field in the southern province of Sindh with estimated reserves of more than one trillion cubic feet.

A government statement, quoting exploration results from the company's Pakistani subsidiary, Lasmo Oil Pakistan Limited, said the disocvery had been made from Bhit-2 exploration well in Kirthar concession of western Sindh.
"According to preliminary estimates, the discovery may contain over one trillion cubic feet of gas," it said. "This will be confirmed through appraisal programs...in hand."

The Kirthar petroleum concession is a joint venture of Lasmo and Shell Exploration Pakistan B.V. having 47.5 percent each and the state-run Oil and Gas Development Corp five percent working interest but with a right to back in for 20 percent on commerciality, the government statement said.
"The (Bhit-2) well has now been suspended and planning is under way for the appraisal of this discovery and evaulation of the greater Kirthar area," it said.
"This will entail a comprehensive seismic survey commencing in 1997, followed by a sustained drilling programme over this and other similar leads available in the concession area."

The statement said well-testing was contrained by "limits of the test equipment" and resulted in a cumulative flow rate of 17.7 million cubic feet per day of gas from three zones. "The produced gas contained no hydrogen sulphide, minor amounts of carbon dioxide and approximately 20 percent nitrogen."
It quoted Lasmo's chief operating officer Johan Hogan as saying his company was delighted with Bhit-2's success.

"The well has confirmed the presence of an excellent hydrocarbon province and increased the attractiveness of several other prospects in the area. We are now well placed to add further to this success through our planned seismic acquisition and drilling program."
